note: Warfare's 115 technologies in the row schema of technologies.json. Keys are written without zin_tech_. Equipment and sub-unit ids come from the warfare spec lists: an archetype zin_<name>_equipment has variants _0 to _5, a hull zin_hull_<name> has variants _0 and up, convoy and train_equipment and motorized_equipment keep their engine keys. Where the spec table lists a person, 'Volgan' is country:Volgan and 'the_dead' is never matched by people (Zol is hidden from every row but its own). Names avoid the words of banned_words.json (a key may still say steel or corps).

technologies.name: Iron Arms
technologies.desc: Spears, swords and axes of forged iron, in the hands of levies and trained foot alike. Every realm with a smith can arm a host.

technologies.name: Forged Iron
technologies.desc: Smiths fold and hammer the iron until it is tougher and takes a keener edge.

technologies.name: Tempered Iron
technologies.desc: Quenched in water and drawn back in the coals, a blade keeps its edge and does not snap.

technologies.name: Pattern-Welded Blades
technologies.desc: Rods of hard and soft iron are twisted and welded into one bar. The blade bends but does not break, and its pattern shows the smith's name.

technologies.name: The Master Forges
technologies.desc: The great forges of the realm are given to masters who answer to no one for their methods, and their blades are the best the age has seen.

technologies.name: Mountain Iron
technologies.desc: Ore from the deepest mountain seams makes iron so clean that a blade made of it outlasts three owners.

technologies.name: Hunting Bows
technologies.desc: Hunters' bows of yew and ash arm companies of archers who can loose a dozen shafts before the foe closes.

technologies.name: Composite Bows
technologies.desc: Horn, sinew and wood are glued into one short bow that outshoots the plain stave and can be drawn from the saddle.

technologies.name: War Longbows
technologies.desc: Archers drilled from boyhood draw staves as tall as themselves, and their volleys darken the air above a field.

technologies.name: Crossbows
technologies.desc: A stock, a lath and a trigger: any levy can be taught to shoot a bolt that pierces mail at fifty paces.

technologies.name: Windlass Crossbows
technologies.desc: A winding crank spans the strongest lath, and the bolt goes through plate. The crank is slow, and that is the price.

technologies.name: Mail Shirts
technologies.desc: Thousands of riveted rings make a shirt that turns a blade. Heavy foot can stand where light foot would break.

technologies.name: Plate and Mail
technologies.desc: Iron plates cover the chest, head and limbs, with mail where a joint must bend.

technologies.name: Full Plate
technologies.desc: Shaped plates, fitted to the man, cover him from crown to heel, and a wearer who is properly trained can move as freely as in cloth.

technologies.name: Tempered Plate
technologies.desc: Plate that has been quenched and tempered stops a bolt at close range, and armourers sign each piece in gold.

technologies.name: Masterwork Plate
technologies.desc: A suit that takes a master a full year to make is worth a village, and the lords who own one do not lend it.

technologies.name: Shield-Wall Drill
technologies.desc: Foot are taught to lock shields rim to rim and hold the line while the second rank thrusts over their shoulders.

technologies.name: Hill Companies
technologies.desc: Men of the high valleys are formed into companies that climb where hosts cannot march and hold the passes.

technologies.name: Sea Soldiers
technologies.desc: Soldiers drilled to fight from a deck and to land through surf, ready to storm a quay from the cogs that bring them.

technologies.name: Ranger Craft
technologies.desc: Foresters who can track, hide and shoot are formed into bands that fight best where the land is wild.

technologies.name: Pike Squares
technologies.desc: Ranks of long pikes make a hedge no horse will charge, and the same square can advance behind its points.

technologies.name: Veteran File-Leaders
technologies.desc: Old soldiers with scars to show lead each file and keep the line closed when the first rank falls.

technologies.name: Elven Arms
technologies.desc: Slender blades and long bows, made by elven hands from wood and metal that were old before the Fourth Age began.

technologies.name: Leaf-Forging
technologies.desc: Elven smiths forge blades as thin as a leaf, light enough to lift with one finger and strong enough to cut mail.

technologies.name: Elven Mastery
technologies.desc: After centuries of practice, a master's arms are made once and last as long as the wood grows.

technologies.name: Forest Rangers
technologies.desc: Wardens of the green wood, who walk unseen beneath the trees and strike when the foe is far from his road.

technologies.name: The Sun Guard
technologies.desc: The towering folk of the sunlit south form their guard: few in number, slow to rouse and nearly impossible to break.

technologies.name: Warband Iron
technologies.desc: Rough iron, quickly made, for war bands that count on numbers and fury.

technologies.name: Blackened Iron
technologies.desc: Blades blackened in the pit-fires hit harder and are meant to be wielded in the dark.

technologies.name: Valley Wardens
technologies.desc: The temple's small guard of valley wardens, sworn to keep the roads and shrines in peace.

technologies.name: Riding Horses
technologies.desc: Sturdy mounts bred for the saddle carry riders across the open lands faster than any host can march.

technologies.name: War Horses
technologies.desc: Great horses, bred for weight and trained to stand under the din, can bear a rider in mail through a line of foot.

technologies.name: Great Studs
technologies.desc: The crown founds great studs where the best stallions are kept and the best mares sent, and a finer breed of warhorse follows.

technologies.name: Remount Depots
technologies.desc: Fresh horses wait at every depot along the roads, so a rider never has to ride a dying mount.

technologies.name: Destriers of the Plains
technologies.desc: Over generations the herds of the open plains are crossed with the great studs, and the result is a mount of strength and wind that no other breed matches.

technologies.name: Camel Host
technologies.desc: In the dry lands riders go to war on camels, which cross sands and thirst that would kill a horse.

technologies.name: Horse Archery
technologies.desc: Riders who shoot from the saddle at a gallop and wheel away before the foe can answer.

technologies.name: The Couched Lance
technologies.desc: With the lance held under the arm and the whole weight of horse and rider behind its point, a charge breaks a line outright.

technologies.name: Elven Steeds
technologies.desc: Slender horses that answer to a word, trained by the elves to run without road or rein.

technologies.name: Raider Mounts
technologies.desc: Wiry mounts, half tamed, carry orc raiders far across the border before the alarm can be raised.

technologies.name: Troll Brood
technologies.desc: The troll broods bring their brutes to the war-moot, each wrapped in hide and swinging an iron-bound club.

technologies.name: Ogre Pacts
technologies.desc: Chieftains bargain with the ogre clans for brutes who will fight beside the warbands for plunder.

technologies.name: Giant Kin
technologies.desc: The giants rouse their kin to war, a few huge hosts and a few great hurlers who fling boulders over walls.

technologies.name: The Moots
technologies.desc: When the ents decide to walk, a grove walks with them. They decide slowly, and cannot be turned back once they have.

technologies.name: Yeti Hunts
technologies.desc: The great hunts of the frozen north become war-bands, furred, tireless and unaffected by the cold.

technologies.name: Kin Harness
technologies.allowRaw: OR = { has_tech = zin_tech_troll_brood has_tech = zin_tech_giant_kin has_tech = zin_tech_ent_moots has_tech = zin_tech_yeti_hunts has_tech = zin_tech_ogre_pacts }
technologies.desc: Smiths learn to shape plates and straps for the great kin, and their gear no longer breaks at the first hard blow.

technologies.name: Kin Mastery
technologies.desc: Generations of work with the great kin give their gear a fit and a weight that no earlier smith could have found.

technologies.name: Catapults
technologies.desc: Frames of timber and rope fling stones over walls. A host with catapults need not wait for a gate to open.

technologies.name: Torsion Engines
technologies.desc: Twisted skeins of sinew store the strength of many men. They fling heavier stones and shoot long bolts that pierce the hide of monsters.

technologies.name: Counterweight Trebuchets
technologies.desc: A long arm, a sling and a box of stones: the trebuchet throws a heavy stone further and harder than any engine before it.

technologies.name: Scorpions
technologies.desc: Bolt-throwers on swivels, aimed upward at whatever flies. They guard towers and camps against the winged.

technologies.name: Siege Towers and Rams
technologies.desc: Wheeled towers and iron-headed rams carry sappers to the foot of a wall and over it.

technologies.name: Fire-Pots
technologies.desc: Clay pots of burning pitch burst over a camp or a rooftop, and the fire does the work that stones cannot.

technologies.name: Great Engines
technologies.desc: Engines as tall as a hall, built by crews that do nothing else, and their throw is heard in the next valley.

technologies.name: Engine Crews
technologies.desc: Standing crews of engineers, carpenters and teamsters keep the great engines working and the host's stones flying.

technologies.name: Master Engines
technologies.desc: Master engineers refit every engine of the realm with better skeins, better frames and better aim.

technologies.name: Stone Forts
technologies.desc: Stone walls, towers and gatehouses let a few hold a pass or a harbour against many.

technologies.name: Layered Walls
technologies.desc: An outer wall, a ditch and an inner wall: an attacker who breaches one finds another behind it.

technologies.name: Harbour Chains
technologies.desc: A chain across the harbour mouth, raised by a windlass, closes the port to any hull that does not fly the right flag.

technologies.name: Wall Wardens
technologies.desc: Garrisons that do nothing but guard a wall learn every stone of it, and no attack takes them by surprise.

technologies.name: Bastions
technologies.desc: Angled towers that jut from the curtain let defenders shoot along the foot of every wall, so there is no blind ground to shelter an assault.

technologies.name: Curtain Walls
technologies.desc: Long walls link tower to tower and fort to fort, until a whole frontier can be held as one work.

technologies.name: Field Healers
technologies.desc: Healers follow the host with herbs, bandages and clean water. Fewer wounded die and more return to the line.

technologies.name: Lantern Wards
technologies.desc: Lanterns of ward-glass, blessed tokens and the old words say how to hold off what the dead cannot be hurt by.

technologies.name: Hallowed Arms
technologies.desc: Blades and spear-heads washed in blessed water and marked with the sign of warding. The dead feel them, if only a little.

technologies.name: Wards Against Death
technologies.desc: The highest wards that men have learned: a circle drawn, a name spoken and the shapes of the dead are held back for a time.

technologies.name: Wardsong
technologies.desc: The elves sing over their arms in the old tongue, and what they sing is a ward that the dead remember.

technologies.name: The Old Songs
technologies.desc: Songs older than the Fourth Age steady the elves in battle, and they do not give way before what is hard to look upon.

technologies.name: Grave Binding
technologies.desc: Rites of the south bind the fallen to their weapons and set them marching again. They need no bread and do not tire.

technologies.name: Necromantic Orders
technologies.desc: Orders of robed masters keep the rites alive, mend the fallen between battles and raise new hosts from the slain.

technologies.name: Deeper Rites
technologies.desc: The masters descend into older rites, and the grave hosts they raise stand firmer than any before them.

technologies.name: Grave Riders
technologies.desc: Horses that have died and risen carry riders who have done the same, and the two never tire.

technologies.name: Nether Pacts
technologies.desc: Pacts struck below the earth call the Netherborn to arms, each bound by an oath that ends only with death.

technologies.name: Nether Forges
technologies.desc: Forges fed by the heat of the deep earth hammer out weapons that no mortal smith could have shaped.

technologies.name: Bound Demons
technologies.desc: Demons held to service by binding oaths, who fight where they are sent and nowhere else.

technologies.name: The Deathless Tide I
technologies.desc: The first stirring of the Old God's dead in the Mistake: shapes that stand because he wills it.

technologies.name: The Deathless Tide II
technologies.desc: The tide runs stronger. The dead rise in greater numbers and hold their shapes against the blows of mortal arms.

technologies.name: The Deathless Tide III
technologies.desc: At the full flood of the tide, the dead are no longer shapes at all, and nothing mortal can end them.

technologies.name: Scouts
technologies.desc: Light riders and runners range ahead of the host, find the foe and the fords, and lead the column home.

technologies.name: Sappers
technologies.desc: Diggers and carpenters bridge rivers, clear roads, undermine walls and raise palisades in a single night.

technologies.name: Wagon Trains
technologies.desc: Long strings of ox-wagons carry grain and stores along the high roads, a season's march in one column.

technologies.name: Supply Columns
technologies.desc: Pack-animals and drovers feed the host from the depots, and its supply no longer depends on the nearest village.

technologies.name: Heralds and Beacons
technologies.desc: Heralds with horns, flags and beacons carry orders along a line of march and tell each captain what the others are doing.

technologies.name: Quartermasters
technologies.desc: Officers who count every sack and every nail and see that the host eats before it fights.

technologies.name: Provosts
technologies.desc: Provosts keep order in camp and in taken towns, hang looters and hold the peace of the roads behind the host.

technologies.name: Armourers
technologies.desc: Armourers with portable forges mend broken weapons on the march, and gather what the foe has dropped.

technologies.name: The High Roads
technologies.desc: Raised and paved roads link the great towns, and wagons run on them in any season.

technologies.name: Winter Quarters
technologies.desc: Stout huts, stacked wood and warm food let a host winter in the field without losing a man in ten.

technologies.name: Water Caravans
technologies.desc: Skins and casks of water follow the column across dry country, and the heat takes fewer men.

technologies.name: War Camps
technologies.desc: Standing camps behind the front keep recruits drilled and ready, and gaps in the line are filled within days.

technologies.name: Field Kitchens
technologies.desc: Cooks with copper pots follow the host and feed it hot meals, and the sick list grows shorter.

technologies.name: Great Depots
technologies.desc: Storehouses the size of castles hold a campaign's grain, and the host can march a whole season from them.

technologies.name: Oared Galleys
technologies.desc: Narrow hulls driven by rows of oars, with an iron-shod ram at the prow, and fast enough to catch anything that sails.

technologies.name: Merchant Cogs
technologies.desc: Broad, deep-bellied cogs carry grain, timber and iron from harbour to harbour.

technologies.name: Harbour Works
technologies.desc: Quays, moles and wharves that shelter the fleet and speed its repairs, with masthead lookouts to spot a sail before it spots you.

technologies.name: Sailing Warships
technologies.desc: High-sided hulls under canvas carry heavier bolt-throwers than any galley and can keep the sea in rough weather.

technologies.name: The Triton Charts
technologies.desc: The island-folk's charts of tides, currents and star-bearings give a captain the sea lanes that were once their secret.

technologies.name: War Galleys
technologies.desc: Galleys built for war, with banks of ballistae, benches for stronger oarsmen and a mast for the long haul.

technologies.name: Corsair Craft
technologies.desc: Lean, dark hulls that lurk in coves and strike the cogs of rivals before slipping out to sea.

technologies.name: High-Castled Warships
technologies.desc: Fighting castles at bow and stern give archers the height to shoot over any rail, and a deck of catapults shatters hulls at range.

technologies.name: Boarding Parties
technologies.desc: Picked fighters, hooks and gangplanks turn any hull into a landing craft or a floating fortress.

technologies.name: Deep-Water Hulls
technologies.desc: Hulls deep and broad enough to cross the open sea, with ocean cogs to carry a host over the wide water.

technologies.name: Fireships
technologies.desc: Hulls packed with pitch and brush, steered into a crowded anchorage and set alight.

technologies.name: Bronze Sheathing
technologies.desc: Bronze plates below the waterline stop rot and borers, and a sheathed hull rams and is rammed with less harm.

technologies.name: Great Warships
technologies.desc: The greatest ships of the age: three decks, three masts, decks of war-engines and crews of hundreds, the flagships of a realm's fleet.

technologies.name: Storm Rigging
technologies.desc: Extra stays, double sheets and storm sails let a fleet ride out gales that would drive older ships onto the rocks.

technologies.name: Warded Hulls
technologies.desc: Hulls marked with the old wards and hung with blessed lanterns, so that what climbs up from the dark water finds no purchase.

technologies.name: Master Shipwrights
technologies.desc: The greatest builders refit every class of hull, and a navy at last has ships that match its sailors.

technologies.name: Elven Hulls
technologies.desc: Hulls of grown wood with sails the shade of dawn, which catch every breath of wind and need little rest.

technologies.name: Eyries
technologies.desc: High stone roosts on cliffs and towers, where griffins are bred, fed and trained to carry a rider.

technologies.name: Griffin Harness
technologies.desc: A saddle that fits the beast and a rider who can trust it: the first harness light enough for a griffin to fly in.

technologies.name: Sky Lances
technologies.desc: Long lances, balanced for a rider in flight, let a griffin knight strike at another beast from above.

technologies.name: Dragon Lore
technologies.desc: What the elves know of the dragons of the high mountain: their moods, their ways and the pact that lets one fly at their side.

technologies.name: Dragon Kinship
technologies.desc: A bond of long trust between rider and dragon makes each one bolder in the other's company.
